nodes.summary: A predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is counter-machine decidable when some counter-machine program computes its characteristic function: for every natural number $n$, the output of the program on the single input $n$ is defined and equals $1$ if $P(n)$ holds and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Counter-machine decidable predicates

nodes.summary: The output of a counter-machine program $p$ on a list of inputs is the partial natural number obtained as follows: run $p$ from the initial state on those inputs; if for some number $t$ of steps the program counter is at least the length of $p$ (the machine has halted), the output is the content of register $0$ after the least such $t$; if no such $t$ exists, the output is undefined.
nodes.title: Output of a counter machine

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a counter-machine program, $s$ a state, and $t_1 \le t_2$ natural numbers. If the state reached from $s$ after $t_1$ steps of $p$ has program counter at least the length of $p$, then the state reached from $s$ after $t_2$ steps equals the state reached after $t_1$ steps.
nodes.title: Counter-machine execution is constant after halting

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a counter-machine program, $s$ a state and $t$ a natural number. If the state reached from $s$ after $t$ steps of $p$ has program counter at least the length of $p$, then the state reached from $s$ after $t + 1$ steps equals the state reached after $t$ steps.
nodes.title: Counter-machine execution is stable once halted

nodes.summary: For a counter-machine program $p$, a natural number $t$ and a state $s$, the execution of $p$ for $t$ steps from $s$ is the state obtained from $s$ by applying $t$ single steps of $p$.
nodes.title: Bounded execution of a counter machine

nodes.summary: The initial counter-machine state on a list of inputs $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ has program counter $0$, register $i$ holding $x_i$ for each $i < k$, and every other register holding $0$.
nodes.title: Initial state of a counter machine

nodes.summary: A counter-machine instruction is one of: increment register $r$, decrement register $r$, or jump to instruction $q$ if register $r$ is zero, where the register index $r$ and the jump target $q$ are natural numbers.
nodes.title: Counter-machine instructions

nodes.summary: A counter-machine state consists of a program counter, which is a natural number, and the register contents, a function assigning a natural number to every register index $i \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Counter-machine states

nodes.summary: Past the end of the program the state does not change.
nodes.title: A counter step is sticky at halting states

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a counter-machine program, a list of instructions indexed from $0$, and let $s$ be a state with program counter $c$. If $c$ is at least the length of $p$ (the machine has halted), the step leaves $s$ unchanged. Otherwise it executes instruction $c$ of $p$: increment register $r$ adds $1$ to register $r$ and sets the program counter to $c + 1$; decrement register $r$ subtracts $1$ from register $r$ if it…
nodes.title: One step of a counter machine

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a counter-machine program, let $x$ be a list of natural-number inputs, and let $t$ and $y$ be natural numbers. If the state reached after $t$ steps of $P$ from the initial state on $x$ has program counter at least the length of $P$ (so the machine has halted) and register $0$ holds $y$ in that state, then the output of $P$ on $x$ is defined and equals $y$.
nodes.title: Output membership for counter machines

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
